- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices; apply a 1–2% upward bias for final 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to align with sentiment momentum.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of price decline), model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
